rules.checkpoint_sequence: zero for a root and parent sequence plus one for every child; siblings may share a sequence
rules.named_head_revision: independent non-negative CAS revision; never inferred from checkpoint sequence

execution_semantics.logical_turn: one caller input and one outward result across one or more execution segments
execution_semantics.execution_segment: one private recoverable provider, tool, or suspension interval within a logical turn
execution_semantics.internal_provider_completion: commit a private provider-boundary checkpoint before dispatching a requested tool
execution_semantics.structured_input: reference the existing portable continuation by ID, revision, digest, execution definition, and revision binding; never copy its provider snapshot
execution_semantics.outward_completion: commit a completed-outward-turn checkpoint and public mapping atomically

rules.stream_allocation: a provisional ID may appear in non-terminal stream events but is not retrievable or resumable
rules.commit: checkpoint bytes, public mapping, and ID state commit in one atomic boundary
rules.terminal_event: response.completed is emitted only after both checkpoint and public ID are committed
rules.commit_failure: withhold the public mapping, quarantine completed upstream state, preserve the parent, and return state_commit_failed
rules.publication_failure: do not redispatch; reconcile the committed mapping by idempotency identity or authorized retrieval

response_resource.store_false_terminal: publish a committed opaque response ID with no addressable mapping after the transient processing boundary
response_resource.store_true_terminal: publish only after the durable authorized mapping and checkpoint commit atomically

normalization.endpoint: lowercase scheme and host, remove default port and trailing slash, retain only stable path components

existing_type_references.portable_continuation: PortableContinuation by ID, state revision, and digest through PortableContinuationReference; payload and provider_snapshot are excluded

lane_identity.canonical_serialization: domain-separated length-prefixed UTF-8 fields in declared order
lane_identity.multiple_models: each stable model slot produces a distinct lane ID within the same outward response

provider_lane_binding.drift: reject before dispatch with typed binding_drift; explicit visible-transcript reset creates a new lane and reports opaque-state loss
provider_lane_binding.opaque_state: never merge, compare, or replay across lane IDs

ordinary_child.result: new immutable child on the parent's branch

explicit_branch.result: new immutable child with a new branch ID

named_head.success: expected_head_revision equals current revision; atomically point the head to the committed child and increment once
named_head.conflict: mismatch performs no checkpoint, mapping, outbox, task, or head write

idempotency.intentional_branch: use the branch operation and a distinct canonical request digest; never reinterpret a conflicting continuation as a branch
idempotency.provider_idempotency_key: transport metadata only; it is not provider deduplication proof

storage.permitted_pairs: all Cartesian pairs allowed by server policy and capability; provider stored always requires explicit disclosure
storage.served_store_false: transient local processing only; bounded operational metadata cannot reconstruct provider state
storage.served_store_true: durable authorized public mapping and checkpoint required
storage.mode_conversion: explicit reset or conversion only; stored parent IDs and stateless ledgers never overlap
storage.stored_parent_compaction: unsupported until an explicit stateless fork operation is defined

retention.effective_ttl: minimum of each applicable local TTL, envelope TTL, and known upstream lifetime
retention.unknown_upstream_lifetime: returns no guaranteed effective TTL even when local or envelope TTLs are known
retention.provider_stored_status: must be unknown or known; known requires a positive TTL
retention.non_stored_status: must be not_applicable and cannot carry an upstream TTL

descendants.self_contained_child: remains usable after parent local expiry or deletion when it owns every required immutable blob reference
descendants.provider_stored_child: fails closed with upstream_ancestry_unavailable when required provider ancestry expires or is deleted
descendants.deleted_parent: cannot create new descendants after tombstoning; already committed children retain their independent lifecycle
descendants.content_addressed_blob: delete only after the final committed checkpoint and reconciliation reference is released; a missing referenced blob is checkpoint_corrupt

deletion.ordering: authorize, atomically tombstone local access and enqueue upstream deletion, then retry the outbox independently
deletion.partial_failure: keep the response unusable and report safe upstream deletion status; never restore local access
deletion.constant_disclosure: lookup, continuation, compact, retrieve, branch, and delete conceal wrong authority, absent, expired, and tombstoned targets

migration.cutover: atomic schema and authority change; exactly one provider-state writer; no dual-write authority
migration.provider_binding_change: proven migration or explicit visible-transcript reset

configuration.request_rule: may narrow but never increase storage, retention, capabilities, branch limits, concurrency limits, or provider storage

authority.local_single_user: fixed_local_single_user only when explicitly configured and not network exposed
authority.authorization_order: authorize scope before disclosing existence, lifecycle, or equality

surfaces.deferred_field_policy: omit unsupported stateful fields or reject them before dispatch; never accept and discard
